title: Agencies request comment on proposed rules to strengthen capital requirements for large banks

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve, FDIC, and OCC jointly requested public comment on a proposal to implement the final Basel III capital standards (Basel III endgame), which would apply to banks with $100 billion or more in assets. The proposal would standardize credit risk, market risk, operational risk, and financial derivative risk measurements, require inclusion of unrealized securities gains/losses in capital ratios, and is estimated to increase aggregate common equity Tier 1 capital requirements by approximately 16 percent for affected bank holding companies.
key_points: Proposal applies to banks with $100 billion or more in total assets; community banks excluded
Estimated 16 percent aggregate increase in common equity Tier 1 capital requirements for affected bank holding companies
Banks would be subject to supplementary leverage ratio and countercyclical capital buffer if activated
Unrealized gains and losses from certain securities would be required in capital ratios
Transition period: implementation begins July 1, 2025, with full compliance by July 1, 2028
Separately, a proposal to adjust GSIB capital surcharge methodology would measure systemic importance averaged over the entire year rather than only year-end value
why_it_matters: This regulatory proposal establishes the framework for how large banks will calculate and hold capital, directly affecting bank profitability, lending capacity, and systemic risk resilience. The 16 percent capital increase estimate would impact the largest, most complex banks most significantly. Market participants need to monitor how these requirements affect bank balance sheets, cost of capital, and competitive dynamics between large and community banks.
macro_context: The proposal was issued in response to March 2023 banking turmoil and aimed to implement the final Basel III agreement components while applying stronger capital requirements to a broader set of large banks.
market_structure_context: The proposal represents a structural change to bank capital regulation, implementing Basel III endgame standards and addressing lessons from March 2023 banking turmoil. The GSIB surcharge adjustment and countercyclical capital buffer provisions add additional macroprudential tools to the regulatory framework.

issues_found: Source is approximately 2 years and 8 months old (from July 2023), beyond the 90-day threshold, but has clear archival value as a historical regulatory benchmark

notes: Historical regulatory proposal from July 2023. The Basel III endgame capital rules have since been finalized and the July 2028 full compliance date has passed relative to TODAY (April 2026). This source captures the original proposal phase and estimated 16% capital increase figure. Source quality is high (Federal Reserve, FDIC, OCC joint release) but age limits relevance for current market structure analysis.
